title: Sift potting soil through a two-handled garden sieve over a tub, keeping the pebbles in the sieve
instruction: Sift the soil into the tub, keeping the pebbles in the sieve, and leave the sieve resting on the battens.
context: Gardeners, landscapers and nursery workers (O*NET 37-3011.00 Landscaping and Groundskeeping Workers; 45-2092.00 Farmworkers and Laborers, Crop, Nursery, and Greenhouse), and home gardeners, sift soil and compost before potting and sowing to take out stones and lumps, resting the sieve on two battens across a barrow or tub. Full of soil it is lifted by its two handles and shaken level over the tub until the soil has gone through the mesh; the stones stay in the sieve, and nothing may go over the rim, or unsifted soil and stones end up in the sifted soil. This sieve is wider than a gripper opens, with a flat handle on each side, so it takes both arms to lift it off the battens, shake it and set it back level: lifted by one handle it stays propped on its other side, and rocked that way it either walks off the battens into the tub or sifts too little.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. A fixed green garden tub, 28 x 28 cm inside and 6 cm deep with 1 cm walls, stands centred at (40, 0). Two fixed pine battens, 2 x 32 x 1.2 cm, lie across its left and right rims at x 28.8 and 51.2. On them rests a loose square garden sieve (600 g), centred at (40, 0) with its mesh 7.2 cm above the table: a beech frame 20 cm square inside and 7 cm tall (front and back walls 2.4 cm thick, resting on the battens; side walls 8 mm) over a steel mesh of 4 mm square bars with 14 mm square holes, and a flat black handle 6 x 2.5 x 1 cm out of the middle of each side wall (y 10.8 to 13.3 and -10.8 to -13.3), 2.5 cm above the mesh. On the mesh lie 216 g of soil, 72 loose crumbs (2 x 1 x 1 cm sticks, 3 g each) in two layers over its middle 15 cm square, and six loose grey pebbles, 2.6 cm across and 30 g each, which settle among the soil at (33, -5), (45, -5), (39, 3), (38, 7), (49, 7) and (44, -9). The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot. A real trial uses 216 g of damp potting soil prepared the same way each time (compost rubbed through a 10 mm sieve, air-dried for two days, mixed with half its mass of water and kept in a closed box; see the README), spread evenly over the mesh about 1.5 cm deep, with the pebbles at those spots.
scoring: In the simulation every body's pose is read after each control step (20 Hz) and each gripper's centre from its arm's joints. Soil counts only once it has gone down through the mesh: each crumb is followed in the sieve's frame from inside the sieve (above the mesh, inside the walls) to below the mesh; a crumb that leaves over a wall is never credited, and the crumbs that drop through while the scene settles count as through the mesh. The score is 0 for the rest of the run, overriding any credit earned before, once any pebble has left the sieve (its centre outside the walls: lifted out, onto the table or into the tub) or once any soil has left the sieve over its walls. Otherwise, at the end of the run, by the mass of soil through the mesh and in the tub as a share of the 216 g at the start: 0.25 for 25 % or more (54 g; 18 of the 72 crumbs); 0.5 for 50 % or more (108 g; 36 crumbs); 1.0 for 70 % or more (151.2 g; 51 crumbs) with all six pebbles in the sieve and the sieve resting back on the battens (its middle within 2 cm of where it started and within 1.5 cm of its starting height, tilted less than 6 degrees), let go (both grippers' centres 3 cm or more from every part of it) and still, for 2 s. Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: the overhead and wrist videos show whether any pebble or soil left the sieve over its walls (0); after the run all the soil inside the tub is brushed into a tared bowl and weighed on a kitchen scale (1 g steps), and its mass against the 216 g weighed onto the sieve gives the same levels (54 g, 108 g, 151.2 g); a tape measure and a phone level check the sieve's position and tilt on the battens.
reset_notes: Put the sieve back on the battens at its marks. Real trial: gather all the soil (from the tub, the sieve, the battens and the table) back into the closed box of prepared soil, empty the tub, weigh 216 g of the soil onto the mesh and spread it evenly about 1.5 cm deep, and lay the six pebbles on it where the screenshot shows them; nothing is consumed. In the simulation each trial starts the simulator afresh (each inspect-robots run does).
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX (Isaac Sim 6.1), 20 Hz control. The soil is 72 rigid 2 x 1 x 1 cm sticks of 3 g: round crumbs smaller than the holes would drop straight through, while damp soil passes only when shaken; the sticks lie across the bars until shaking tips them end-first through a hole. Crumbs and pebbles get gentler contact settings, as the engine otherwise flings pieces jammed between bars out of the sieve. The simulation tracks each crumb through the mesh; a real trial weighs the tub's soil.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both arms stayed back near their bases, the right gripper lowering toward the table beside the tub; neither came within 16 cm of the sieve, which was never touched); demo: 1.0
